script.title: Offer vs Invitation to Offer
script.caption_hook: A price tag is not a promise! Offer vs invitation to offer, explained.

lines.say: Price tag on a shirt, yet the shopkeeper can refuse to sell?
Yes, he can. A price tag is only an invitation to offer. First, what is an offer?

board.title: Offer or Not?
board.sub: Price tag is not a promise

lines.say: Okay, so what exactly is an offer?
You show willingness to be bound once they say yes. That intention is the test.
It only asks others to make offers. You may accept or refuse them. Accepting it makes no contract.
Then in a shop, who makes the offer?
The customer. At the counter, he offers to buy at the tag price. The shopkeeper accepts, or refuses.
Oh! So the display just invites. What about auctions?
Same idea. The auctioneer's announcement invites. Your bid is the offer, and the fall of the hammer is acceptance.
Hmm, so is every advertisement only an invitation?
No. A reward advertisement is a general offer. Performing the condition accepts it, as in Carlill's case.
Got it! Tags, catalogues and tenders only invite offers.
